claims.claim: The paper reports comparable performance to the full dataset under its fixed-initialization experiments.
claims.limitations: The distillation procedure, emotion labels, source corpora, privacy threat model, model initialization, and UAR evaluation bound the claim; smaller data is not automatically private or representative.

claims.claim: The paper reports that NSIM maps phoneme-recognition performance and is sensitive to simulated degeneration, suggesting a candidate noninvasive biomarker.
claims.limitations: Auditory-periphery model, task, simulations, participant data, and mapping assumptions bound clinical interpretation; a candidate biomarker is not a validated diagnosis.

claims.claim: High-feature participants were less accurate for neutral speech and high-intensity happy speech, with distinct confusion patterns and marginally higher confidence for angry speech.
claims.limitations: Mandarin synthetic stimuli, university participants, self-report grouping, F0 manipulation, and perceptual task bound generalization; the findings do not diagnose BPD or explain all underlying causes.

claims.claim: The proposed CE-ViViT approach achieved modest-error decoding, with speaker-normalized contours decoded more accurately than raw contours in the reported experiments.
claims.limitations: Participants, Mandarin tones, EEG sessions, normalization rule, model, and modest-error metric bound the neural claim; better decoding does not by itself reveal the full perceptual code.

claims.claim: On VoxCeleb1, the paper reports EERs of 1.29%, 1.60%, and 2.80% on the O/E/H trials and relative improvements over prior self-supervised methods.
claims.limitations: VoxCeleb1, trial conditions, unlabeled-training setup, score normalization, and EER bound the claim; benchmark gains do not establish fairness or robustness in deployment.

claims.claim: On IEMOCAP and MELD, the paper reports up to 4.0 and 3.7 absolute UAR gains over the relevant baselines and presents descriptors as explanations.
claims.limitations: Datasets, descriptor definitions, LLM/SSL choices, bottleneck size, and benchmark labels bound the interpretation; a predicted descriptor is not automatically a human-valid cause.

claims.claim: The paper reports 68.5% MELD accuracy, 0.93 Fleiss kappa, 83% human rationality ratings, and a 131.2-hour benchmark with up to 26 emotion types.
claims.limitations: Video sources, model judgments, cultural assumptions, label taxonomy, human validation, and downstream use bound the claim; agreement or rationality is not ground-truth emotion.

claims.claim: The system reports 8.09% diarization error rate on the challenge evaluation set and first place in the MISP 2025 diarization task.
claims.limitations: Challenge data, channel layout, scoring convention, enrollment assumptions, and test conditions bound generalization; rank and DER do not guarantee usable transcripts in every meeting.
